themes_detail.label: Wildlife Crisis in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal complaints in UWS parks spiked to 14 THIS WEEK, up 367% from the 3.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.33), signaling a sudden and severe wildlife management problem that poses potential safety and public health risks.
evidence: 14 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly baseline (8-week average)
367% spike with z-score of 7.33 — statistically extreme deviation
Spike is brand new; no prior sustained elevation in this complaint category
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about what species are being reported and whether there's been a change in wildlife management or habitat disruption
Canvass park users and nearby residents about what animals they've encountered and when incidents occurred; identify which parks are hotspots

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped to 13 LAST WEEK, up 154% from the 5.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.75), indicating a rapid deterioration in street condition and possible organized dumping or enforcement gaps.
evidence: 13 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
154% spike with z-score of 6.75 — statistically extreme deviation
Suggests either a recent event (major dumping) or enforcement/towing capacity breakdown
reporting_angles: Identify which streets or blocks have the most abandoned vehicles; map the geographic pattern
Contact NYPD and Department of Sanitation to determine if there's been a towing service delay or increased illegal dumping activity

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Building Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about violations outside buildings spiked to 4 THIS WEEK, up 700% from the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95), pointing to possible encroachment, obstruction, or safety hazards on sidewalks and building exteriors.
evidence: 4 outside-building violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
700% spike with z-score of 4.95 — statistically extreme deviation
New signal; no pattern of elevation prior to this week
reporting_angles: Pull 311 complaint details to determine what specific violations are being reported (scaffolding, awnings, trash, construction debris, etc.)
Contact Department of Buildings to assess whether there's been a spike in unpermitted construction or a change in enforcement priorities

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Intensify
themes_detail.summary: Violations of park rules complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, up 300% from the 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.24), suggesting disorder, unauthorized activities, or inadequate Parks Department enforcement in green spaces.
evidence: 4 park-rules-violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Converges with animal complaints spike, suggesting broader park safety and management issues
reporting_angles: Investigate what specific park rules are being violated (off-leash dogs, trespassing, unauthorized vendors, etc.) by reviewing 311 complaint narratives
Assess whether Parks Enforcement Patrol presence and staffing levels have changed recently

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 15 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 118% from the 6.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.43), indicating a recent environmental or air pollution event that may warrant further investigation.
evidence: 15 air quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 6.9 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Peak is slightly older than animal/vehicle spikes; current status unclear
reporting_angles: Determine whether the air quality spike correlates with a specific incident (construction, traffic, wildfire smoke) or ongoing industrial activity
Cross-reference with EPA or NYC Department of Environmental Protection air monitoring data for the UWS during that week
